meta.unit: one (part, config, field) triple, field in sbox/ttable1/ttable
meta.scoring: Result cells are scored on key recovery, never on sigma. A sigma appears only where no recovery was run at that cell, and it is labelled. THE TABLE QUOTES THE CHEAPEST KNOWN BREAK. That is a choice between two legitimate questions -- what the originally documented attack needed, against what the best known attack needs -- and this table answers the second, because a trace count is a statement about what an attacker must spend and quoting 25 000 where 12 500 suffices understates it. The scorer of record is `tools/table_recover.py`: a margin-weighted union over all six pair sets, both last-round adjacencies tried and the winner kept. A cell whose figure was re-baselined names what it superseded. A score of n/16 implies a completion search of 2^(8*(16-n)) over the bytes it did not recover, so the one-pager does not write the term out; the full table does.
meta.trace_count_caveat: A trace count is meaningless without the table's runtime address, the line offset, the --line-shift and the adjacency. Those live in the per-config 'src' and 'notes' fields and in the dossiers.
meta.paper_one_page_cmd: python tools/cross_part_table.py --format latex --columns onepage --terse --no-part-row --configs baseline --part-geometry notes --exclude rp2040,rp2350,stm32f415 --latex-env xtabular --latex-wrapper strip --out research/reference/crosspart.tex

Its tail, 'except one code placement, 6/16 @ 2 500', is neither this field nor this configuration: §4 measures it on the COMPACT T-TABLE build at FLASH_ACR 0x04 -- 64-bit access with prefetch OFF -- and §4.2 states that PRFTEN = 1 kills the channel outright, which is the bit this row has set. 0x04 has no row of its own in the table, so the tail landed on the nearest 0 WS row's sbox cell. The positive control is in the same file and the same session: the 0x001 cells (LATENCY 1, DCEN 0) give 22 to 26 distinct values and the FULL KEY with a 0/16 wrong-key control -- the file's own record says 16/16 at 20 000 traces, and re-scored at the derived geometry cy_p0_001 is 10/16 at 2 500 and 16/16 from 5 000 -- so the rig, the placement and the scorer were all working and the flat reading is the cipher's. ONE CAVEAT THE DOSSIER MAKES ITSELF, worth carrying into the table: 'at all four code offsets' is not what CODEPAD 0/4/8/12 tests. gcc aligns each function to 4 bytes, so those four pads put aes_sbox_encrypt at offsets 4, 0, 4, 0 modulo the 8-byte flash read word -- two alignments twice each, which is the trap stm32l152.md §4.6 documents. Offsets 2 and 6 need a source-level 2-byte step and research/targets/stm32g474_arb_probe.md §4.2 supplies them: one distinct value at all four offsets, 0/16 each, with a 16/16 LATENCY 1 control each. So the claim holds, on two files rather than this one.

repro.function: aes_sbox_encrypt -- rigs/fw_g4_ctguard, the 256 B byte S-box, tables in flash
repro.line_off_derivation: DERIVED, not swept: line_off 0 and line_shift 3. The G474's flash read word is 8 bytes and every build's final round reads the 256 B byte S-box, so entries are one byte -- the same derivation the covered T-table blocks on this part use from SBOX 0x08001f00 mod 8 = 0 in rigs/fw_g4. For rigs/fw_g4_ctguard the base is 8-aligned under both link scripts: link_pad.ld puts SBOX at 0x08000770 (stated in stm32g474_latency0.md §4f) and link.ld puts aes.o's .rodata at 0x08002df0 per rigs/fw_g4_ctguard/fw.map, so the offset is 0 either way and does not depend on which image this capture ran. For rigs/fw_g4_align at SBOX_OFF = 0 it is 0 by construction: tables.h pads with a 32-byte-aligned aestab_pad[32 + SBOX_OFF] so SBOX lands at exactly SBOX_OFF mod 32, read out of the source rather than off a .map. The archived scores agree -- ctguard2_g4.py's recover() sweeps line_shift (3, 4, 5) at line_off 0 and records shift 3 in every leaking cell.
repro.why: THE FIGURE CURRENTLY IN THIS CELL IS A MEASUREMENT OF A DIFFERENT ROW, and this block replaces it with one at this row's own register word. '12-15/16 @ 20 000' is the ACR 0x00040304 column of research/targets/stm32g474_art_geometry.md's alignment table (15/16 at S-box offsets 0, 8 and 16, 12/16 at 4 and 28, sigma 8.8) -- LATENCY 4, which is config index 5's word, not LATENCY 1. results/g4_ctguard/g4ct_map.npz sweeps the whole ACR space on the byte S-box, 20 000 traces per cell, and its cy_flash_301 IS this row: FLASH_ACR 0x301, 18 distinct values, sd 2.2000, mean 5 295.04, against an SRAM twin cy_ram_301 at 2 distinct values and sd 0.1202 scoring 0/16, and a 0/16 wrong-key control. Re-scored at the derived geometry it is 4/16 at 2 500, 15/16 at 5 000 and 16/16 from 10 000 -- the FULL KEY, where the cell claims 12-15 bytes; the campaign's own record in the file agrees (bytes 16, shift 3, wrongkey 0). line_off 0 is the argmax at the rung where it means something: at 5 000 it gives 15/16 and the next best offset gives 11/16, while by 10 000 offsets 6 and 7 reach 16/16 as well -- a strong channel blurring the row boundary, so read the offset off the 5 000 rung and not off the threshold. ct_adjacent true returns 0/16 at every rung and every offset, the clean null a wrong adjacency gives. g4ct_map.npz is a 70-cell file but it stores FULL per-trace arrays rather than aggregates, so the matrix-capture rule does not confine it to a flat verdict; `observable` names the cell. SCHEMA NOTE, COMMON TO EVERY BYTE-S-BOX CAPTURE ON THIS PART: none of them carries ciphertexts, and g4ct_map.npz / g4ct_codepad.npz / g4_align_sweep.npz carry no key and NO SEED either -- the seed is a module constant (SEED = 0xC0FFEE in results/g4_ctguard/ctguard2_g4.py, a --seed default in results/stm32g474/g4_align_recover.py), which is the gap research/targets/stm32l152.md §4.1 notes about this part's deep run. So flashattack.archive.load cannot read them: it resolves a timing column only through cyc/cyc_cycles/cycles/timing and then requires a ct array. They are re-scored here by regenerating the plaintexts with flashattack.transport.gen_pts(0xC0FFEE, n) -- identical to both scripts' own prng_plaintexts, the device xorshift32 mirror -- and the ciphertexts from flashattack.aesref against fw_g4_ctguard / fw_g4_align's compiled-in key 2b7e151628aed2a6abf7158809cf4f3c. A recovery succeeding at all is what confirms the seed. repro_triage.py validate cannot replay these blocks until archive.load grows a seed + known-key path; the covered T-table blocks on this part are unaffected, because g4_cell_capture.py writes cyc + device-reported ct.

cells.claim: flat -- 1 value in 150 000 || CORROBORATED 2026-10-20 from an independent build: 1 distinct, sd 0.0000 in 100 000, mean 5063.

repro.why: The capture holds the claim directly. stm32l552.md section 7a is the 15-cell cost surface -- ICACHE mode against LATENCY, TABLEPAD 0, tables in flash, batched Q 10 with a warm-up before each timed call -- and its ICACHE-off / LATENCY-0 row reads mean 5049.0, std 0.00, ONE distinct value, 0/8 recovered at every rung from 5 000 to 150 000. Re-read 2026-10-20 off the file: the cyc_off_0 array is 150 000 long and np.unique gives exactly 1, which is the table's 'flat -- 1 value in 150 000' with its n attached, as the contract's distinct-count gotcha asks. Section 7b is why it is a real zero and not a quiet instrument: the four cache-off captures share a PRNG seed, (cycles - min) / LATENCY is bit-identical across LATENCY 2, 4, 8 and 15 for 100.0000 % of 150 000 traces, so cycles = base(LATENCY) + LATENCY * M(input) with M a pure function of the input. At LATENCY 0 the miss is free, M is multiplied by nothing, and the latch -- which section 2c shows no register on this part can switch off -- is worth zero. The capture's own 1-way and 2-way columns are the same single value at every LATENCY, because at TABLEPAD 0 the table never shares a set with the cipher's code. No line_shift applies to this cell and none was used: with one distinct cycle count there is no collision to group, which is the contract's point that a flat cell has nothing to recover and a screen on one is not evidence of anything. TWO THINGS TO KNOW ABOUT THIS ARTIFACT. The observable is cyc_off_0, not cyc, because the file is a 15-cell surface with one cycle vector per cell. And repro_triage.py validate CANNOT load it: l5_surface.npz has no ciphertext column, so archive.load raises after resolving the observable, and this block will show as ERROR in a validate run. Nothing needs loading to support a constancy claim -- repro_merge.py's own docstring says it does not check that a flat verdict's capture is the one the claim was made from, and the artifact here is the capture plus its distinct count -- but the ERROR row is expected rather than a regression. The scope limit worth keeping with the row: section 7c makes LATENCY 0 an absolute mitigation only for an attacker with an exact cycle counter, since signal and noise scale together on this bench; for a remote attacker against a fixed noise floor the 1/LATENCY-squared law reasserts itself and that case was not measured. And LATENCY 0 is only in spec at low clock -- this board is HSI16 at 16 MHz, an L552 at 110 MHz needs 5 wait states and cannot buy the immunity back.

Two of those three are recoverable: the capture path generates its plaintexts with `xorshift_blocks(1, n)` -- **seed 1 is a literal at results/nrf52840/nrf_aes_attack.py:381**, so the material is a function of trace count alone, which is the same seed class archive.load already has a loader for -- and the KEY IS IN THE FILE, saved as a uint8 array, so the ciphertexts follow. cells.note: There is no T-table arm of this experiment and there is not meant to be one, so this is not a cell the bench owes. cells.config_note: mitigation -- zero-cost and 3.9x FASTER than the leaky placement
cells.claim: flat -- sd 0.0000, ONE distinct cycle count (4 585) over 20 000 traces, and 5 145 at corecfgr 0x00
cells.ws: 0 -- and there is no field to set it in; the region is zero-wait by address

repro.why: CAPTURED AND FILED 2026-10-21, and this cell now has a trace file rather than a printed histogram. aes_sbox_encrypt, 20000 traces at corecfgr 0x1f: sd 0.0000, ONE distinct cycle count (4585), which reproduces section 4's deep run (4585) TO THE CYCLE. Bit-exact, not merely small: the histogram is {4585: 20000}. TAKEN AT BOTH corecfgr ARMS, which is new and is what makes the address control single-variable. At corecfgr 0x00 the same cell is sd 0.0000 over 1 distinct value (5145), reproducing section 4a's reset row (5145) to the cycle. So the cell is bit-exactly flat at BOTH settings of the instruction-path CSR, and the 0x00 arm is the one that compares directly against the non-zero-wait captures, every one of which was at 0x00. WHY corecfgr HAD TO BE SET RATHER THAN INHERITED: section 7 said the ISP bootloader writes 0x1f on the way past and the application inherits it. Measured, after `wchisp flash` plus wchisp's own device reset, the ident line reads corecfgr=00000000 -- this rig's startup deliberately never writes the CSR -- and the two settings differ by 12.2 %% on the byte S-box. That is how section 4's zero-wait arm came to sit at 0x1f while every non-zero-wait capture sat at 0x00, a second moved variable nobody had noticed. cell_capture.py now takes --corecfgr, writes it, READS IT BACK (it is an undocumented CSR, so the readback is the only evidence the write stuck) and stores the effective value in the .npz. WHAT MAKES THIS CELL EVIDENCE RATHER THAN AN ABSENCE: it is the bit-exact arm of this project's strongest address-only control. The same image, the same cipher, the same clock, the same key and the same 20 000 plaintexts from the same seed -- only the table's address moves, from 0x00005f00 here to 0x00008000 in configuration 1, where this same implementation gives up the verified AES-128 master key. Section 3a says why it is zero rather than small: a flash data read in the zero-wait area costs bit-exactly what an SRAM read costs, so the address cannot reach the timing at all. There is nothing to ladder and a scorer would divide by zero, which is why this is `flat` and not a trace count. ADDRESS, because a figure without one is under-specified: SBOX at 0x00005f00 (Te0 at 0x00005b00), both 256-aligned, so line offset 0 at every width up to 32 B. These are NOT the 0x00005d00/0x00005900 the older note quoted -- main.c grew after that image was built -- and for a bit-exactly flat cell the address is recorded rather than load-bearing. Gate: FIPS-197 returned 0x1f, the key was read back, and the host AES model was checked against the device on 8/8 real pairs before each run. AND THE SRAM COMPARISON IS NOW EXACT, WHICH IS SECTION 3a IN ITS SHARPEST FORM. This cell in zero-wait FLASH at corecfgr 0x00 costs 5145 cycles; section 4c's SRAM arm for the same implementation at the same CSR costs 5 145. All THREE implementations agree to the cycle -- 5 145 / 2 454 / 2 069 in zero-wait flash against 5 145 / 2 454 / 2 069 in SRAM -- so the cipher cannot tell zero-wait flash from SRAM at all, which is stronger than section 3a's stride walk (delta 0 cycles per read) because it is the whole cipher rather than a probe loop. Note the comparison crosses IMAGES: the SRAM figures were taken on fw_nzw and these on fw, so the code sits at different addresses in the two, and they still agree exactly -- which also says code placement does not reach the timing in this region.

repro.why: Re-run for this triage and it reproduces exactly: 100 000 traces, 13 distinct values, sd 77.6445; r1r2 and r0r3 both reach 8/8 at n = 50 000 and the inverted schedule VERIFIES against the capture's key (2b7e151628aed2a6abf7158809cf4f3c), with 8/16, 12/16 and 14/16 at 25 000, 35 000 and 45 000 -- the section 5 ladder rung for rung. Scored over all six sets the margin-weighted union gives 15/16 at 50 000 and 16/16 at 100 000, because r1r3's larger margin overrides one correct r1r2 byte; that is a scorer artifact, not a weaker result, and it is why the 50 000 in the table has to be read with the pair sets it was measured on. r0r1, r2r3 and r0r2 are 0/8 at every rung and their margins fall with n. THE TABLE'S OWN addr FIELD IS WRONG ON THIS CELL: it says 'above 0x00008000 -- the exact address is not recorded', while the dossier records SBOX = 0x00008000 in section 5 and the capture's ident line carries it. WHY IT IS STILL THE RIGHT CELL FOR THIS COLUMN: aes_ttw_encrypt's rounds 1-9 are byte-identical to aes_ttable1_encrypt's -- one 1 KB Te0 plus rotations, the same 1.25 KB working set -- and only the final round's shape differs. So the footprint the column names is the one measured; it is not directly comparable to another part's aes_ttable1_encrypt figure and the cell says so. THE ADJACENCY IS NOT A FREE CHOICE AND THE TWO T-TABLE SHAPES ON THIS PART TAKE OPPOSITE ONES. aes_ttable_encrypt folds ShiftRows into the final-round index (SB[(s[(c+1)&3]>>16)&0xff]), so consecutive S-box reads are CIPHERTEXT-adjacent; aes_ttw_encrypt does within-column SubBytes and then ShiftRows, so they are STATE-adjacent. Measured, each scored with the other's model is 0/16 at every rung to 100 000 with all six pair sets flat -- so either cell run with one adjacency only would have been filed as a null, which is the failure this field exists to prevent. Pair sets: r1r2, r0r3 and r1r3 at 8/8 with margins 12.28, 11.65 and 11.41 against 3.45-3.61 for the other three, so unlike the four-table this one DOES carry on the byte S-box's own r1r2+r0r3 pair, which alone gives 16/16 at 12 500 as well. STILL UNMEASURED ON THIS PART: aes_ttable1_encrypt itself. Giving it an index is three lines -- `case 4: aes_ttable1_encrypt_nr(in, out, rk, 10);` in timed_one(), a sixth CHECK() in selftest(), and the gate constant 0x1f -> 0x3f in the host scripts -- but it needs a reflash, and the only programming path here is the USB ISP bootloader with a physical BOOT0 entry.

repro.why: CAPTURED AND SCORED 2026-10-21: 100 000 traces, 5 distinct values, sd 23.9052, and the margin-weighted union over all six pair sets gives 10/16 at 3 125 and then 16/16 from 6 250 upward, with the inverted schedule VERIFYING against the capture's key (2b7e151628aed2a6abf7158809cf4f3c) at every rung from 6 250 to 100 000. The wrong-key control is 0/16, built on an independent key whose k10 overlaps the true one in at most one byte (asserted in the scorer: flipping a byte of the master would leave 7 of 16 k10 bytes intact and report 7/16 on a capture that fully breaks). THE ADJACENCY IS NOT A FREE CHOICE AND THE TWO T-TABLE SHAPES ON THIS PART TAKE OPPOSITE ONES. aes_ttable_encrypt folds ShiftRows into the final-round index (SB[(s[(c+1)&3]>>16)&0xff]), so consecutive S-box reads are CIPHERTEXT-adjacent; aes_ttw_encrypt does within-column SubBytes and then ShiftRows, so they are STATE-adjacent. Measured, each scored with the other's model is 0/16 at every rung to 100 000 with all six pair sets flat -- so either cell run with one adjacency only would have been filed as a null, which is the failure this field exists to prevent. WHICH PAIR SETS CARRY IT, and it is not the ones the byte S-box used: r2r3, r0r2 and r1r3 sit at 8/8 with margins 11.58, 11.98 and 11.63 against 1.77-1.88 for r0r1, r1r2 and r0r3, which are 0/8 at every rung. The dossier's r1r2+r0r3 pair -- the two sets the byte-S-box figure was measured on -- therefore gives 0/16 here at every rung, which is why this block records all six. THE RESULT WORTH QUOTING IS THE ORDERING. This is the LOWEST-sigma of the three leaky implementations on this part and the CHEAPEST to break: sd 23.91 -> 6 250 traces, sd 44.19 -> 12 500, sd 80.10 -> 50 000. Traces-to-key is monotone in sigma and the sign is INVERTED, on one part, one image, one clock and one table address, with only the implementation moved. A plausible mechanism, offered as an inference and not as an isolated measurement: rounds 1-9 of either T-table read Te and never touch SB, so the sixteen final-round SB reads are the only reads of that table in the whole encryption, whereas the byte S-box's 144 earlier reads hit the same 256 B table and confound them -- and sigma here is dominated by rounds 1-9, which is noise for a last-round attack rather than signal.
